incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: THALIA-429-high — sustained 429s from tenant=thalia-prod in dedicated pool. Paging oncall rota: Maria.
Maria (oncall): acked — jumping in. any customer-facing impact right now?
Alex (AM): Thalia reporting timeout + 429s to their live traffic. Support says spikes since ~09:12 UTC. They're seeing failed requests in critical path.
Maria (oncall): logs show 429s from our gateway for 2xx of their requests. Attaching quick sample.
Maria (oncall): ```
2026-03-15T09:12:03Z gateway request_id=abcd tenant=thalia-prod status=429 upstream_pool=shared-fallback
2026-03-15T09:12:07Z gateway request_id=abce tenant=thalia-prod status=429 upstream_pool=shared-fallback
```
Jess (TAC): that upstream_pool looks wrong — thalia should be pinned to dedicated_thalia pool. Did we recently migrate them?
Sam (sre): there was a routing config rollout earlier this morning (09:00 UTC) to refresh tenant->pool mappings. suspect config race. I'll check route-manager logs.
Devin (infra): checking autoscaler events + pool health. If they got evicted from their dedicated pool and routing fallback kicked in, that might explain 429s due to quota on shared pool.
Sam (sre): route-manager log snippet: ```
[09:11:58] route-manager INFO reload config v=2026-03-15-09-00
[09:11:59] route-manager WARN tenant=thalia-prod assigned_pool=shared-fallback (missing dedicated entry)
```
Alex (AM): customer is P1 Critical for them — they want immediate mitigation. Can we do emergency contract override/unthrottle while we fix routing?
Maria (oncall): options: 1) emergency quota override for tenant (temporary unthrottle) 2) reassign tenant to dedicated_thalia pool (if capacity free) 3) roll back routing config. Best short-term: emergency override + attempt to reassign to dedicated pool.
Jess (TAC): I can run override via admin API. Command I use: ```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://admin.internal/api/v1/tenants/thalia-prod/overrides" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"type":"rate_lift","reason":"emergency customer impact","expires_in_s":7200}'
```
Maria (oncall): do it and confirm response. add expiry 2h. Also set an ops annotation so billing/compliance knows this was emergency.
Jess (TAC): done — API returned 200 + override_id=ovr-78f3. Customers should stop getting 429s once gateway honors it. Pushing annotation now.
Jess (TAC): ```
{"status":"ok","override_id":"ovr-78f3","expires_at":"2026-03-15T11:12:23Z"}
```
Devin (infra): I'm seeing queue depth drop a bit but still some 429s. Looks like requests are still landing on shared-fallback where quota is low. I'll try to force-assign thalia to dedicated_thalia if capacity available.
Devin (infra): checking pool capacity... dedicated_thalia has 2 spare slots. Attempting assign.
Devin (infra): ```
# k8s patch tenant assignment
kubectl patch tenant thalia-prod -p '{"spec": {"pool": "dedicated_thalia"}}' --type=merge
```
Sam (sre): route-manager picked it up and routing table updated. Logs: ```
[09:14:12] route-manager INFO tenant=thalia-prod assigned_pool=dedicated_thalia via patch
```
Maria (oncall): monitoring metrics: 429 rate for thalia-tier dropped from 18% -> 1.5% in last 3m. latencies stable. :thumbsup:
Alex (AM): passing update to Thalia's CTO — said they'd like an ETA for root cause and timeline for permanent fix.
Jess (TAC): I've created incident ticket INC-429-THALIA and added override details, operator steps, and rollback note.
Sam (sre): root cause hypothesis: routing config reload earlier dropped the dedicated mapping due to a race when config generation omitted a cached entry. Follow-ups: will add guard in route-manager to not fallback if dedicated assignment previously existed and capacity available.
Devin (infra): follow-up work: add unit test for config generator + autoscaler handshake to reduce eviction->fallback window. I'll estimate 2 sprint points.
Maria (oncall): action summary: 1) emergency rate-lift applied (ovr-78f3) 2) forced assign to dedicated_thalia 3) monitoring + customer updates in progress 4) follow-up tickets opened (INC-429-THALIA, RTE-2026-rm-fix).
Alex (AM): Thalia acknowledged update and asked for a postmortem. Please include timeline and billing note for emergency override.
Sam (sre): will own postmortem. I'll gather logs and timeline.
Maria (oncall): will stay on watch for 30m then handoff to Sam for postmortem work. If error rate creeps back up, we re-open paging.
Jess (TAC): marking this thread resolved for immediate customer impact — continuing follow-up in INC-429-THALIA. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident THALIA-429-high acknowledged and status set to mitigated by Maria at 2026-03-15T09:16:03Z. PagerDuty note added.
